blocks.text: To survive, every animal must sense and respond to changes in its surroundings, and the activities of its organs and systems, such as heart rate, breathing and digestion, must be coordinated so that each is regulated to the body's needs.

items: Nervous coordination, controlled by the nervous system, using electrical signals.
Chemical coordination, controlled by the endocrine system.

blocks.text: In nervous coordination the nervous system coordinates the body with the external environment and coordinates the different parts of the body with each other, by means of electrical signals. This chapter deals with the human nervous system.

blocks.title: Think of a city
blocks.text: Think of the body as a large city. For it to run smoothly, traffic lights, emergency services and power plants must all talk to each other; this talking is coordination.
